result_json.message: docs: add plan review for OpenCode 2.x upgrade

items.title: Tie settlement to delivery of the submitted prompt
items.reason: V2 prompt admission returns an inbox item, while execution terminal events identify only the session. The prior turn can emit a terminal event before the new prompt is delivered.
items.failure: A resumed invocation can settle against the previous execution, return the wrong reply or usage, or send a summary prematurely.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Require delivery evidence for the exact inbox item before settling either path; reject an active or overlapping session when ownership cannot be established. Add a same-session prior-terminal-before-delivery regression.

items.title: Cancel pending work as well as running work
items.reason: Session interrupt does not remove a queued inbox item, and an aborted admission request can have committed before its acknowledgment is received.
items.failure: A cancelled external invocation can execute later, or interrupt a different execution.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Short-circuit a pre-aborted turn, assign a stable prompt ID before admission, and bound the RPCs. Cancel the owned pending item or interrupt the owned active execution, handling a delivery race. Add delayed-acknowledgment and queued-cancellation fixtures.

items.title: Route headless forms by their actual session discriminator
items.reason: The planned data.sessionID filter drops form.created, which carries sessionID and id under data.form.
items.failure: The headless fallback ignores its own pending form and the invocation stalls.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Extract the nested form session and ID, test own and foreign forms, and explicitly exercise question denial or the fallback in the live test.

items.title: Use an executable Phase 1 unit-test gate
items.reason: The Phase 1 review records nonzero exit from bare bun test test/unit on both revisions, and a passing run with the configured parallel flags.
items.failure: The literal required Phase 1 command cannot provide passing evidence on the reviewed tree.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Spell the previously passing configured unit command in the gate: bun test --concurrent --parallel=2 --dots --timeout 15000 test/unit.

items.title: Pipe managed stderr explicitly
items.reason: Bun inherits stderr by default for the specified spawn, which contradicts the bounded diagnostic capture and draining contract.
items.failure: Early startup errors lose the required stderr tail and child diagnostics bypass managed capture.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Specify piped stdout and stderr in the managed spawn options and assert both in the existing spawn-seam test.

items.title: Exercise real reviewer output through 5x invoke
items.reason: AC1 includes author and reviewer results, but the live provider schema and end-to-end invoke checks exercise only the author role.
items.failure: Both modes can pass the acceptance suite even if neither returns a CLI-validated reviewer verdict.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Seed a valid temp plan/run and run one unrecorded reviewer invoke in each existing mode fixture, checking role-specific ReviewerVerdict validation alongside the author checks.

items.title: Require positive live evidence for the advertised minimum
items.reason: The enabled live suite can skip on an unsuitable binary, and a test only on 2.4.2 does not verify the claimed 2.4.0 minimum.
items.failure: The release can claim compatibility with an unverified minimum or pass the opt-in gate without exercising either mode.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Fail bad prerequisites when opted in, require both cases on the advertised minimum or raise it to the oldest verified release, and align the old-2.x error with that minimum and the doctor upgrade hint.

result_json.summary: The W7 re-estimate is credible and DC0 is eligible at plan time, but the prior inherited-budget blocker is a CLI governance matter, not an estimate correction or a credit-carry guarantee. The plan needs mechanical corrections to turn ownership, cancellation, headless handling, and acceptance evidence before it is executable as written.

baselineAssessment.reason: Independent sizing by implementation boundary: private server/client and event mapper, asynchronous turn and recovery, structured extraction, factory and live validation, installed native delegation and harness sync, doctor, TUI deletion, and release verification. Server timing and the installed delegation exercise are the main uncertainties.

creditAssessments.reason: Removing the old SDK requires addressing its unused importers before provider typecheck. Deleting the retired attach, permission and routing path is simpler than porting it; the persisted phase-1 target and before/after evidence substantiate provisional plan eligibility, not execution carry.

plan(219): v1.5 address plan review R7–R13 (review of 13a626a8)

Verified OpenCode 2.4.2 inbox/delivery/cancel/form behavior via client
declarations and live probes; prompt ownership with delivery-gated and
overlap-safe settlement (R7), owned bounded cancellation (R8), form
session routing (R9), runnable Phase 1 unit gate (R10), explicit managed
stdio pipes (R11), reviewer 5x invoke acceptance (R12), and verified
minimum-version evidence (R13). Ledger: new W9 (5) and W10 (1), W8 3 -> 5.

result_json.notes:
Plan v1.5 addresses R7–R13. Before writing the R7 and R8 design, I checked the @opencode/client 2.4.2 declarations and ran two live probes against a local OpenCode 2.4.2 server.

Two findings changed the design:
- A prompt sent while the session is running is delivered into that same execution, even with `delivery: "queue"`. So the turn refuses a busy session up front and treats other input during the turn as an ambiguous error, never a success.
- `inbox.cancel` returns success for unknown and already-delivered prompts. So cancellation decides from server evidence whether the prompt was removed or delivered, and only interrupts a running execution that holds this turn's prompt alone.

Polling now settles on the durable transcript `idle` entry after the prompt, which keeps the R3 early-failure path.

Delivery Budget changes:
- New W9 (5) covers R7 and R8. The combined work is about 4, which is off-scale, so it is scored 5 and split from W7 to stay at or under 8.
- New W10 (1) covers R12.
- W8 goes from 3 to 5 for R9 and R13.
- W7 adds R7, W1 adds R11, W3 adds R10, and W6 adds R7, all with scores unchanged.

Rows total 34 against baseline 26, which may exceed the current standard ceiling of 33. The revision history says so, and no estimate was lowered. Phase 1's checked items and commits are preserved; R10 changed only the gate command text. The reviewer's nonblocking follow-ups were not taken on as tracked work. `5x plan phases` reports executable true and budget.ok true.

result_json.message: docs: update plan review for OpenCode 2.x upgrade

items.title: Tie settlement to delivery of the submitted prompt
items.reason: The revised delivery gate excludes prior terminal events, but polling can miss a prompt delivered between the transcript and inbox reads. The cumulative usage read after settlement can also include a replacement execution not covered by the overlap flag.
items.failure: A valid delivered turn can be misreported as cancelled, or a resumed invocation can attribute another execution’s usage to its result.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Do not infer cancellation from separate negative reads; recheck delivery on an inbox miss. Use usage scoped to the owned reply window or fail closed when it cannot be attributed, and add regressions for both races.

items.title: Cancel pending work as well as running work
items.reason: Stable IDs and bounded cleanup help, but an unknown-item cancel is a no-op and a delayed POST may still enqueue. The session-wide interrupt has no execution discriminator; an activity check is not atomic with it.
items.failure: A cancelled prompt can enqueue after cleanup declares it removed, or cleanup can interrupt another client’s replacement execution.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Reconcile uncertain admission within the cleanup bound and report uncertainty without claiming removal; do not resend after cancellation. Use session-wide interrupt only with separately established exclusivity. Add late-enqueue and replacement-execution regressions.

items.title: Require positive live evidence for the advertised minimum
items.reason: The new positive live gate and error hints are in place, but the Phase 2.2 constant is still 2.4.0, conflicting with the governing Design starting value of 2.4.2.
items.failure: The implementation can copy an unverified minimum from the Phase 2 contract or reject the passing required-version evidence as inconsistent.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Align the literal in Phase 2.2 with the 2.4.2 starting value and retain the positive live gate at the actual advertised minimum.

result_json.summary: R9–R12 are addressed. R7 and R8 still need race-safe ownership and cancellation, and R13 needs the minimum-version literal aligned. The current ledger is credible; implementation inherited-budget admission remains distinct from plan-time provisional credit.

plan(219): v1.6 address closure addendum remaining R7, R8, R13 (review of 1684e990)

Review: docs/development/reviews/.5x-worktrees-219-opencode-2-upgrade-plan-78d6ac-5x-cli-docs-development-plans-219-opencode-2-upgrade-plan-review.md (enforced closure addendum, Nov 27 2026).
- R7: bounded unknown polling state (inbox before transcript, removal only on inbox.cancelled); usage only from the owned transcript window, fail-closed attribution; new race regressions.
- R8: no same-id resend; bounded admission and cancel reconciliation with late-admission re-cancel; session interrupt only on the managed private server, never from session.active(); new regressions.
- R13: MIN_OPENCODE_VERSION literal 2.4.2.
- Budget: W9 5 -> 8 (combined ~7, off-scale); W6 adds R8; W7/W8 notes, scores unchanged.

result_json.notes: Plan v1.6 addresses the closure addendum's remaining R7, R8, and R13 corrections; R9–R12 are unchanged. Design choices cite the @opencode/client 2.4.2 declarations: no event replay cursor, interrupt takes only a sessionID, inbox cancel returns void, and assistant and compaction transcript entries carry optional tokens and cost. (1) R7: polling reads the inbox before the transcript. A prompt found in neither is treated as unknown, not removed; only a received inbox.cancelled event proves removal. An unknown state that lasts 10 s fails closed. Usage now comes only from the turn's own transcript window, from the prompt to its closing idle entry, instead of the session.get delta; a window entry without tokens fails the turn with an attribution error. New regressions cover delivery between reads, unknown beyond the bound, a new execution between the terminal event and the usage read, and fail-closed attribution, plus a live window-usage assertion. (2) R8: the same-id resend is removed. A lost or timed-out admission is reconciled from evidence for up to 10 s and otherwise reported as unresolved. Cleanup cancels by the exact id with bounded reconciliation and re-cancels a late admission. session.interrupt is used only on a managed provider's private server (exclusive by construction, with a per-provider in-flight session guard), never decided from session.active(); external providers never interrupt and report the execution as left running. New regressions cover cancel before a late enqueue and a replacement execution between the activity check and the interrupt, with managed and external variants. (3) R13: the §2.2 literal is now 2.4.2. Budget: W9 rescored 5 → 8; the combined work is about 7, which is not an allowed value, so the score is not rounded down, and the row is not split because it shares one state machine and one fixture. W6 adds R8 to Addresses. W7 and W8 gain notes with scores unchanged. Net +3 effort over v1.5. Phase 1 and DC0 are byte-identical to the previous commit. The pre-commit check passed: executable true, budget ok true. Nonblocking follow-ups were not incorporated.
